segments.source: This guide is for a US kitchen making both real espresso and pour-over with one electric grinder. We included only exact current models with a Coffeedant full review, manufacturer support for both grind ranges, and independent evidence about a consequential compromise. We excluded filter-only grinders, the older Opus and Encore ESP, and machines whose exact US version or evidence did not support this comparison. These are workflow picks, not a blind taste ranking.
segments.context: This guide is for a US kitchen making both real espresso and pour-over with one electric grinder. We included only exact current models with a Coffeedant full review, manufacturer support for both grind ranges, and independent evidence about a consequential compromise. We excluded filter-only grinders, the older Opus and Encore ESP, and machines whose exact US version or evidence did not support this comparison. These are workflow picks, not a blind taste ranking. segments.source: If espresso is the daily drink and pour-over occasional, favor a repeatable espresso return and a catch cup that works with your basket. If light-roast pour-over is the main event, demand independent filter-cup evidence: a manufacturer’s all-purpose claim establishes a grind range, not that the filter cup will satisfy you. The Coffee Chronicler’s Opus 2 sample is the caution here.
segments.context: If espresso is the daily drink and pour-over occasional, favor a repeatable espresso return and a catch cup that works with your basket. If light-roast pour-over is the main event, demand independent filter-cup evidence: a manufacturer’s all-purpose claim establishes a grind range, not that the filter cup will satisfy you. The Coffee Chronicler’s Opus 2 sample is the caution here. [1] [4]

segments.source: The other choice is whether beans stay in a hopper. A filled hopper removes a daily weighing step but makes changing coffees more cumbersome. Single dosing helps keep separate bags separate, though it does not remove every retained ground. If you brew the same coffee for both methods, carryover matters less than return-to-setting effort.
segments.context: The other choice is whether beans stay in a hopper. A filled hopper removes a daily weighing step but makes changing coffees more cumbersome. Single dosing helps keep separate bags separate, though it does not remove every retained ground. If you brew the same coffee for both methods, carryover matters less than return-to-setting effort. [2] [3] [6]

segments.source: Start with the espresso recipe that already works in your machine. Note the exact grinder mark, dose and basket. Then move to your pour-over setting and record that position with the dripper, dose and water recipe. On the return, use those notes as a starting point and dial in again: burr position, bean age and the coffee itself can change the shot. A scale and written recipe are more useful than assuming the same printed mark always yields the same cup.

segments.source: The Encore ESP Pro offers a stepless collar and either timed hopper dosing or single dosing. The Opus 2 uses a single side dial and two dedicated cups. Eureka’s Zero 65 All Purpose uses a large micrometric dial and single-dose kit. All three can change grind range; none removes the need to reset dose and evaluate the next brew. These controls are manufacturer descriptions, not Coffeedant-measured repeatability.

segments.source: When switching between different beans as well as brew methods, a small purge may be sensible. How much depends on the machine and your tolerance for mixed grounds; we have no Coffeedant exchange-retention measurement. Eureka’s published anti-retention claims and the Kaffeemacher sample use different protocols, so neither is a universal promise for your kitchen.

segments.source: Changing grind range regularly means more attention to the chute, catch cup and burr chamber. Use the exact manual, unplug before cleaning and keep water away from electrical parts unless the maker explicitly permits it. Keep the included dosing accessories together; otherwise a fast change becomes a search for the correct cup. The Opus 2 and Eureka are single-dose routines; the Baratza can remain a hopper grinder.
